---
title: "Adding a summary"
---

This is the end-to-end workflow for a new evidence summary, from gathering the evidence to a published page.
The detail for each step lives on its own page; this page is the checklist that ties them together.

A summary is spread across five linked Airtable tables:

| Table | One row per… | Holds |
|-------|--------------|-------|
| **Summaries** | summary | Title, status, school stages, overall rating, "What is it?", evidence statistics |
| **Findings** | specific outcome (e.g. "Sleep (adolescents)") | Outcome domain, impact, evidence quality, plain-language summary, evidence detail, school stages |
| **Moderators** | factor the effect differs by (e.g. Age) | The "How effects differ" section |
| **Recommendations** | strategy | Audience, title, "What this looks like", "Why this works", school stages |
| **References** | citation | The full reference, plus an optional source note |

Every field is explained in [Summary fields](summary-fields.qmd).

## 1. Before you start

1. **Check the exposure isn't already covered.**
   Look at the website's [Teachers page](https://motivation-and-behaviour.github.io/bigger-picture-platform/teachers/) and at the Summaries table in Airtable, including drafts.
   There is one summary per exposure, so new research on an exposure that's already covered goes into the existing summary (see [Updating a summary](updating-a-summary.qmd)).
2. **Check the exposure is in the *Exposure type* dropdown.**
   If it isn't, ask the platform maintainer to add it.
   It needs a change to the platform's code as well as to Airtable.
3. **Don't combine exposures that pull in opposite directions** (for example violent and prosocial media) into one summary.
   The overall rating would cancel out and hide both stories.
4. **Gather the evidence.**
   Use meta-analyses and umbrella reviews of children and adolescents wherever they exist (see [Choosing sources](writing-guide.qmd#choosing-sources)).
   Check the Bigger Picture umbrella review's [complete effects data](https://github.com/Motivation-and-Behaviour/screen_umbrella/tree/main/supplementary_files) (Supplementary File 6) for child- and adolescent-specific estimates of the reviews you plan to use.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Plan the ratings first

It is often easiest to list the outcomes, effect sizes and proposed ratings in a table before you open Airtable.
Rate each outcome with [the rubric](rating-the-evidence.qmd), and you will know how many findings rows you need and what the overall rating should be.
:::

## 2. Create the summary as a draft

In the **Summaries** table, add a row and set:

- **Status**: *Draft*.
  Drafts never appear on the website, so you can work on it over several days.
- **Title**: the display name, usually the same as the exposure type.
- **Slug**: leave it blank.
  The sync fills it in, and it becomes the page's web address.
- **Exposure type**, **Screen content** and **Audiences**.
  Choose *Teachers* in Audiences, and add *Parents* or *Students* only if you will also write recommendations for them.
- **School stages**: every stage the evidence comes from, using the ages in your sources (see [On the summary](writing-guide.qmd#on-the-summary)).

## 3. Add the findings

Add one row in **Findings** for each specific outcome, linked to your summary.
The easiest way is to open the summary (expand the row) and add new records from its **Findings** field.

For each row, set the **Domain**, write the **Outcome**, choose **Impact** and **Evidence quality**, and write the **Plain-language summary** and **Evidence detail**.

- Findings with the same domain are grouped under one heading on the website automatically.
- The domains appear in the order of their first finding in the summary's Findings list, and the findings within each domain keep their list order.
  To change the order, drag the rows within the summary's **Findings** field.
- If the evidence goes in different directions within a domain, add separate rows (e.g. "Language skills: amount of screen time" at −1 and "Language skills: educational programmes" at +1) rather than averaging them.
- If the evidence reports a result separately for a narrower age group, such as a meta-analysis of adolescents only, give it its own row and tick its **School stages** (see [On a finding](writing-guide.qmd#on-a-finding)).
  Leave School stages blank on every other row.
- Comparisons between groups (an effect that differs by age, sex, dose and so on) are not findings.
  They go in the next step.

## 4. Add "How effects differ"

If the evidence shows the effect differs by a factor such as age, sex or dose, add a row in **Moderators** for each factor, linked to your summary.

- Choose the factor from the **Moderator** dropdown.
  Each factor can appear only once per summary.
- Reporting that an effect *didn't* differ is useful too (e.g. "Neither meta-analysis found that the links differed by age").
- If you need a factor that isn't in the list, ask the platform maintainer to add it.

## 5. Add recommendations

Add rows in **Recommendations** for the strategies teachers can use, linked to your summary, with **Audience** set to *Teachers*.
Put one strategy per line in **What this looks like**; the website adds the bullets.
Use **Why this works** to link the strategy back to a finding, and only claim what the evidence shows (see [Recommendations](writing-guide.qmd#recommendations)).
Leave **School stages** blank unless a strategy is only for some stages.

## 6. Add references

Add each source to the **References** table and link it to your summary.

- **Search the References table first.**
  Many reviews are cited in several summaries.
  If the reference is already there, link the existing record to your summary instead of creating a duplicate.
- Write the **Citation** in APA 7 style as plain text, ending with the DOI as a web address (`https://doi.org/…`).
- Keep the summary's References list in **alphabetical order by first author**.
  A reference's position in the list is its number on the website.
  A newly linked reference goes to the end of the list, so drag it into place within the summary's **References** field.
- Use **Source note** for a short description shown next to the reference in "About the evidence", e.g. "Meta-analysis: 62 studies, 451,229 adolescents and adults".
- Put sources that have no citation, such as an unpublished analysis, in **Unpublished sources** on the summary, one per line.

## 7. Finish the summary row

Back in **Summaries**, fill in:

- **What is it?**: a one- to three-sentence definition of the exposure.
- **Meta-analyses**, **Primary studies** and **Participants**, where you know them, and **About the evidence**: two or three sentences on what kind of evidence this is.
- **Overall impact** and **Overall confidence**: your judgement of the bottom line across all the findings (see [The overall rating](rating-the-evidence.qmd#the-overall-rating)).
  Do this last, once the findings are settled.
- **Short summary**: one sentence of at most 160 characters, shown on the overview card.
  If the findings are mixed, say so.
- **Last reviewed**: today's date.

## 8. Check it

1. Work through the [checklist before publishing](writing-guide.qmd#checklist-before-publishing).
2. Check the **Sync status** and **Sync message** fields after the next sync run (overnight, or when anyone presses Publish).
   Drafts aren't published, but the sync still checks them: a draft shows *Draft (not published)*, and the Sync message lists anything that would stop it being published.
   Fix everything listed there.

## 9. Publish it as preliminary

1. Set **Status** to *Preliminary*.
2. Press **Publish** in the summary row, then **Run workflow** on the GitHub page that opens.
   Or wait for the overnight run.
3. After a few minutes, check that **Sync status** says *Published*, then find the summary on the website.

[Publishing and fixing problems](publishing.qmd) explains every Sync status and the most common Sync messages.

## 10. Review

A preliminary summary is live, but readers see a banner saying it hasn't been checked yet.
Let the review team know it's ready.
Leave Status on *Preliminary*: the review team sets it to *Reviewed* once they have checked the ratings and text.
